thread:
sam: heads up — multiple customers reporting p99 spikes on inference API since ~2026-03-16T03:10Z. example req id: req_0a9f6b2c. p95 is up ~20%, p99 jumped ~4x. throwing this into eng-oncall.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-4321 created — severity: high. paging eng-oncall.

maria: thx sam. can you paste the grafana panel + one raw trace for the slow req? which region/model?

sam: grafana: https://grafana.internal/r/abc123 (panel: infer.request_latency.p99, 5m window). trace: https://traces.host/trace/trace-0a9f6b2c. happened from eu-west-1, model: redwood/rlhf-small-v1.

alex: FYI we pushed a change to auth-service at 2026-03-16T03:10:54Z — PR #4552. change: on token miss now do sync JWK/KMS fetch instead of returning stale cached token. deploy log: deploy-bot: auth-service v2.14.1 -> v2.15.0 @03:12 UTC.

ira: grabbing logs from eu-west-1 auth nodes now. seeing repeated KMS timeouts on miss:
```
[03:11:02Z] auth-service: token-miss -> fetching JWK from kms://keys/jwk-rot-1
[03:11:05Z] kms-client: request timeout after 3000ms
[03:11:05Z] auth-service: fallback to direct validate -> latency 3205ms
[03:11:05Z] proxy: request queued behind token retrieval, added 3205ms
```

sam: that lines up — trace shows auth validation taking 3.2s on path for slow requests, then inference itself ~150ms. so p99 dominated by auth misses on a subset of requests.

maria: interesting — grafana panel is a rolled-up histogram with 1m buckets. that makes p99 sensitive to a few long auth misses; but traces show those misses are individual events on node set. question: is the histogram coming from ingress (nginx) or from backend rpc timer? could be double-counting.

alex: histogram is from backend service metric infer.request_duration_ms (server side) aggregated in metrics pipeline. we also emit proxy.request_duration_ms. the dashboard panel uses infer.request_duration_ms histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(...[5m]))) — so it's approximate. traces are raw spans (exact). both valid but measure slightly different surfaces.

ira: also noticed the auth-change added a synchronous KMS call on miss — that makes tail worse but infrequent. a heavy p99 but p95 OK.

sam: customer support already pinged complaining about SLA and billing implications. they want rollback or credit.

maria: immediate mitigation options:
- rollback auth-service to v2.14.1 (safest, quick).
- patch to make KMS fetch async + return cached token for request path (medium).
- add temporary routing to avoid affected auth nodes in eu-west-1 (quick but brittle).

alex: I can rollback now. command: `deployctl rollback service auth-service --to-tag v2.14.1 --env prod-eu` — should be <5m to restore previous behavior. note: will lose the JWK rotation fix; need to coordinate with security.

maria: do rollback and then open a follow-up for proper fix (async refresh + metrics to track token-miss rate). also update alerting to include auth-miss count as a signal so p99 doesn't surprise us.

sam: doing rollback now. running `deployctl rollback ...`

deploy-bot: rollback started by sam for auth-service -> target v2.14.1. link: https://deploys.internal/job/roll-9876

support-bot: support ticket TKT-8274 updated: customer notified we're investigating, proposed rollback.

ira: after rollback I'll validate traces over the next 15m and re-run the p99 panel. recommend adding a one-off panel for `count_over_time(infer.request_duration_ms > 1000ms[5m])` to surface auth-miss spikes.

alex: quick explainer for the dashboard mismatch:
- panel A (grafana) uses histogram_quantile on pre-aggregated histogram buckets from our rollout pipeline -> approx p99 per 1m windows. sensitive to spikes inside the window.
- traces compute exact percentile from sampled spans, but sampling rate is ~1/10 for traces -> may miss some spikes (but when present show exact latency).
so they can diverge. recommended: add a tail-count metric and show both together (p99_approx + tail_count) to correlate.

maria: agree. put that in the postmortem. for immediate customer ask — support: offer pro-rated credit per SLA guidelines and communicate timeline to fix.

sam: rollback finished (deploy-bot reports success). verifying now.

deploy-bot: rollback complete — auth-service at v2.14.1 across prod-eu @03:40 UTC.

ira: validating traces: after rollback, slow auth-miss traces gone in eu-west-1. p99 panel dropped to baseline in next 2 windows. correlating logs.

alex: created GH issue #4561 for async JWK refresh + auth-miss metrics + automated KMS retry with backoff. tagging security for rotation plan.

maria: next steps:
- follow-up postmortem (include root cause: sync KMS fetch on token miss introduced tail, metrics mismatch between histogram rollup and trace sampling).
- add tail-count panel and auth-miss metric to standard dashboard.
- support to propose SLA credit TKT-8274.
- schedule patch for async refresh and add runtime flag to toggle sync fetch.

sam: noted. closing incident here but keeping ticket open for postmortem. thx everyone :thumbsup:
